topics.topic: Whether backup restoration continues StoreHistory or creates a new entity, and how the new entity is created
questions: Does restoring a backup continue the backed-up StoreHistory entity, or begin a new StoreHistory entity for the restored store; if it begins a new entity, who mints it and from which backed-up facts?

When a backup replaces a lost store, is the StoreHistory entity from the backup continued as the same entity, or is a new StoreHistory entity minted from the backup's facts; if it is new, who mints it?

When a backup replaces a lost store, is its StoreHistory the same entity continued from the lost store, or a new StoreHistory for the restored store's new history; if it is new, who creates it and from what, given that Registry neither detects the restore nor makes a second one?

quotes:
The facts of one store's history that no other record holds (R0-89): the last
audit sequence number that history ever wrote (M09; State 2 A15 rule 5) and,
once the import has succeeded, its migration closure (M10). Exactly one per
store history.

Registry has no restore operation (R0-89): the owner puts a backup in the
place of a lost store, outside Registry, and Registry starts on it as on any
store. A restored store therefore holds this record exactly as the backup
holds it — the backup's last sequence number, and its migration closure when
the backup was made after the import, none when it was made before — and
Registry neither knows nor records that the store was restored.

It has no identifier: it is identified by the store that holds it, exactly
one per store, and nothing names it — no answer, no record, no audit entry.
Registry makes it, with no closure and number 0, in the transaction that
makes a new, empty store (State 2 A17 rule 5); it never makes a second one.

A store a backup replaced is in whatever point of this lifecycle the backup
holds (R0-89); it is not a transition Registry makes.

Registry makes daily encrypted backups and checks each one (State 2). It has
no restore operation: when the store is lost, the owner puts a backup in its
place on the host, outside Registry (Explicit exclusions), and Registry
starts on it as on any store. That store begins its own history from the
backup: every change after it is lost, the audit entries with it, and
Registry's guarantees — the log's numbering, the closed import — hold within
each store's history; a store without the migration closure accepts the
import (R0-79). What the owner does around a restore is the owner's and is not
part of this specification, which describes what Registry does.
judgement.why: The restored store begins its own history with the StoreHistory record already contained in the owner-placed backup; copying that record is outside Registry and is not a Registry lifecycle transition or a second mint by Registry.

topics.topic: Whether independently changing StoreHistory facts should be split or justified as one model
questions: Make the model boundary follow the change-axis: either split the independently changed facts or establish that they change together for one reason.

The passage must split the independently changing audit-sequence and migration-closure facts into models aligned with their separate change axes, or replace this rationale with one showing that the facts change together and for one reason.
The passage must split facts with independent change axes into separate models, or state a change-axis under which they change together and for one reason.

quotes:
The two facts change for different reasons — every audit append, and the
one import — but they are kept in one record because they share one scope
and one life, the store's history (R0-89), and no caller reads either apart
from the store it is in. Each is changed only by its own transaction, and
neither changes the other.
judgement.why: The model explicitly combines facts that change independently and for different reasons, while its stated rationale relies on shared scope and lifetime rather than a common change-axis.

topics.topic: Explicit field declarations, types, and optionality for StoreHistory facts
questions: Replace these prose-only facts with explicit field declarations that name every field and state its type, including the migration closure's absence or optionality.

topics.topic: Which StoreHistory facts product actions read and whether reads are returned or internal
questions: Which StoreHistory fact does each named product action read, and does “read” mean that the fact is returned to the caller or only used internally?
